ivy: quick pulse from handoff 4 can we try an 'ownership escrow + baton' pattern for followups? short, enforceable handoff so tasks don't drift :hourglass:
nolan: explain the two parts? escrow vs baton?
ivy: escrow = IC posts a small acceptance window (e.g. 4h) for owner to ACCEPT the task. baton = a short-term drive role (48-72h) that keeps momentum and escalates if needed
rhea: sounds promising. how strict is accept window? many owners are deep in oncall work
ivy: default 4h but tunable per incident severity. if owner can't accept, they can nominate an interim in the thread and mark ACCEPT-LATER with ETA. interim becomes responsible until primary accepts
mike: can ops-bot help? auto-timers and board drafts would make this low-friction
ops-bot: I can create an escrow draft card with ACCEPT/REJECT toggles, start a timer, ping owner at 1h and escalate at timeout. I can also add a "baton" tag with expiry after 72h and ping baton daily. (requires board integration)
rhea: small pasteable block for ICs to use before handoff:
```
ESCROW HANDOFF
- IC: @ic
- Owner: @owner (ACCEPT within 4h or assign interim)
- Deliverable: one line
- ETA: YYYY-MM-DD
- Baton: @baton (48-72h drive)
- Blockers: short
- Recurrence: yes/no
```
nolan: metrics we should track: accept-time, percent accepted within window, baton escalation count, time-to-first-update
ivy: next steps: 1) add escrow-baton snippet to KB (ivy) 2) ops-bot escrow prototype (mike) 3) trial on next week's rota (rhea)
mike: prototyping bot flow, ETA 4 days. will post sample thread when ready
rhea: I'll run the trial and collect examples. aim: reduce dangling remediations and spot repeat signals faster :mag_right:
